answers.how: Fitting the ball's trajectory gives about 1545 px/s², so the scale is 9.8/1545 m/px. The person's height is about 284 px.
At 3.0 s, the fitted ball velocity components are approximately 400 and -174 px/s. Converted their resultant using the gravity-derived scale.
At 3.6 s, the fitted ball velocity components are approximately 368 and 753 px/s. Converted their resultant using the gravity-derived scale.
Tracked the person's head across frames around 4.4 s, measuring approximately 147 px/s, then applied the gravity-derived scale.
Measured approximately 249 px from the ball's bottom to its floor-contact level and applied the gravity-derived scale.
The ball's center moves approximately 73 px horizontally and 150 px vertically; converted the resultant displacement using the gravity-derived scale.
Tracked the person's upper body from 4.00 to 5.00 s, measuring approximately 134 px of displacement, then applied the gravity-derived scale.
Measured the ball's diameter at approximately 40 px and converted using the gravity-derived scale.
